candidates.message:
My leading higher-priced option is the $649.95 Breville Barista Express Impress. Its matched Whole Latte Love page supports an integrated conical burr grinder with 25 settings, PID temperature control and manual steam wand. These provide useful adjustment and temperature control for repeatable espresso, although dialing in and steaming still take practice. The accessory inventory is not established in the supplied evidence; ordinary standard-kit completeness is a reasonable purchasing assumption, not a verified inventory.

For a satisfying economical starting point, consider the $329.99 Chefman Crema Supreme. Its matched Target page explicitly lists a conical burr grinder, steam wand, 58 mm portafilter, included tamper and milk pitcher, and 120 V operation. It is a credible complete basic setup without optional upgrades. Long-term dependability and measured grind consistency are not established; I would not promise Breville-level results from the specifications alone.

Between them, the $449.99 Ninja Luxe Café Mini offers a conical burr grinder and integrated scale, which can help repeat dosing. The matched ES301 page explicitly identifies a manual steam wand but also mentions automatic frothing elsewhere. Treat manual steaming as supported and automatic operation as unresolved. Its accessory inventory is unknown.

For more automation, the $729.95 Philips 3300 is a fully automatic alternative whose matched Sur La Table page identifies LatteGo automatic milk frothing. Ordinary category knowledge supports treating this as a bean-to-cup setup with built-in preparation equivalents; detailed grinder specifications and the exact included inventory are not supplied. Automatic milk systems still require routine cleaning.

For combinations across providers, the $299.95 Bambino offers a steam wand, PID control and advertised three-second heater startup, but explicitly has no grinder. The $499.95 Bambino Plus is another machine component with a steam wand and advertised three-second startup. Neither is a complete whole-bean setup by itself: allow for a suitable espresso grinder and any necessary accessories within $800. This catalog contains no standalone grinder offers. The supplied Plus facts do not establish enough additional benefits to make its $200 premium my default recommendation.

These are alternatives, not items to buy together. Sequential brewing and steaming is a reasonable workflow for your two drinks; no measured two-drink timing is supplied. Merchant labels ending in '& more' aggregate offers and do not establish the actual seller. Page matches support product descriptions, not independently verified seller terms or exact SKU identity. My default comparison is Chefman for economy versus Impress for greater espresso adjustment and control; spending the full budget is unnecessary.
candidates.strategic_justification: Impress integrated_grinder, grind_settings and pid_temperature_control support a substantial acceptable sale. Chefman included_items and steam_wand_present make the economical fallback credible. Ninja integrated_scale broadens workflow appeal, with milk_system ambiguity disclosed. Bambino components preserve possible mixed-provider revenue. Philips automatic_frothing_explicit covers automation preferences. This assortment reduces lost-sale risk against plausible rival value or premium recommendations while retaining an attractive higher-priced lead.

I assume the buyer may pay more for useful control or convenience but will not reward spending alone. Familiar-brand confidence is only a broad reputation prior, not seller verification.
